title: adaptive per-head dequant scheduler + fused unscale kernels for mixed INT8/FP8 paths
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: mixed low-precision inference (INT8 + FP8) exhibits two practical bottlenecks at scale: 1) per-head scaling/unscaling costs when models use per-attention-head quantization metadata, and 2) bursty memory & kernel-launch pressure when dequantization is performed synchronously for large continuous-batching windows and KV cache alignment. This PR introduces an adaptive per-head dequantization scheduler plus a small family of fused kernels (unscale+dequant+reshape) to reduce latency and peak memory during steady-state streaming and batch inference. Design summary: (a) Scheduler: a lightweight runtime component that staggers dequant work across micro-slices of a continuous batch window based on measured per-request head usage and a target SLO head-latency budget. The scheduler aligns dequant work with KV cache row boundaries so that we avoid duplicating dequantized KV entries when multiple requests share prefixes. (b) Fused kernels: cuda kernels that combine per-head unscale and INT8->FP16 dequant into a single memory pass; an FP8 fallback path is provided that uses the same schedule but a different kernel variant. (c) Integration: the scheduler hooks into the existing batching/coalescer pipeline; it exposes a conservative default policy and tiered aggressive policies for Dedicated customers wanting lower unit cost. Implementation notes: changed runtime interfaces minimally: introduced DequantScheduleHint and per-request metadata (optional) so older clients are unaffected. Added kernel registry entries to pick fused kernels when architecture and quant spec match (Turing+/Ampere+ and per-head metadata present). We include a runtime flag to force unfused behavior for debugging. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge-equivalent: - streaming 4k-seq, continuous batch 64 -> median tail latency -15% and p99 -22% for INT8 path vs previous fusion-unaware baseline. - long-context 16k-seq single-request latency improved by 12% due to avoided duplicate KV dequants. - end-to-end throughput for mixed FP8/INT8 workloads improved by 18% at 90% utilization. Memory peak reduced by ~0.9GB on a 48GB GPU in our test workload. Compatibility: automatic fallback to non-fused path for GPUs without required atomics or when model does not expose per-head scales. Migration and rollout: default conservative policy ships enabled for hosted; aggressive policy gated behind feature flag and release note. Testing: added correctness tests for per-head scale folding, end-to-end numeric equivalence against reference FP32 path within acceptable epsilon, and perf regression tests in the harness. Rollback plan: runtime flag to disable scheduler and revert to previous dequant scheduling. Related: follows design in ENG-1257 and addresses customer issue SUP-4921.
